mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a common misconception about straight‑line motion?

options.A: Straight‑line motion means the object moves only in a straight path, even if its speed changes.
options.B: Straight‑line motion can occur only when the object moves at a constant speed.
options.C: Straight‑line motion is the same as circular motion.
options.D: Straight‑line motion cannot happen on Earth because of gravity.

mcqs.answer: Straight‑line motion can occur only when the object moves at a constant speed.
mcqs.explanation: A common misconception is that straight‑line motion requires a constant speed. In reality, straight‑line motion only describes the path of the object; the speed may increase, decrease, or remain constant. Option B states the mistaken idea, making it the correct answer for a misconception check. Options A, C and D are either accurate (A) or unrelated statements, not typical misconceptions.

mcqs.question: A stone tied to a string is swung in a horizontal circle. Why does the stone continue moving in a circular path?

options.A: Because the stone tends to move straight, and the string constantly pulls it toward the centre (centripetal force).
options.B: Because the stone’s speed keeps increasing, forcing it to turn.
options.C: Because gravity pulls the stone toward the centre of the circle.
options.D: Because the string pushes the stone outward, keeping it in a circle.

mcqs.answer: Because the stone tends to move straight, and the string constantly pulls it toward the centre (centripetal force).
mcqs.explanation: An object in motion naturally continues in a straight line (Newton’s first law). The string provides a centripetal force that continuously pulls the stone toward the centre, changing its direction and keeping it in a circular path. Option A correctly describes this reasoning. Option B is incorrect because speed does not need to increase; option C confuses gravity with the horizontal centripetal force; option D reverses the direction of the force (the string pulls inward, not pushes outward).

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes rotational motion from straight‑line motion?

options.A: In rotational motion every point of the object travels in a circular path around an axis, while in straight‑line motion all points travel along the same straight path.
options.B: Rotational motion occurs only in liquids, whereas straight‑line motion occurs only in solids.
options.C: In rotational motion all points have the same speed, but in straight‑line motion speeds can differ.
options.D: Rotational motion does not involve any force, while straight‑line motion always requires a force.

mcqs.answer: In rotational motion every point of the object travels in a circular path around an axis, while in straight‑line motion all points travel along the same straight path.
mcqs.explanation: Rotational motion involves every point of the object moving around a common axis on circular trajectories; straight‑line motion has all points moving along one straight line. Option A captures this essential difference. Option B is false; both types occur in all states of matter. Option C is incorrect because points at different radii in rotational motion have different linear speeds. Option D is wrong because forces (e.g., torque) are involved in rotational motion, and straight‑line motion can occur without a net force if the object moves at constant velocity.

mcqs.question: A pendulum swings back and forth, returning to the same position every 2 seconds. Which statement about this motion is correct?

options.A: The motion repeats at irregular intervals.
options.B: The motion repeats after equal intervals of time called the period.
options.D: The motion only occurs in living organisms.

mcqs.answer: The motion repeats after equal intervals of time called the period.
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion is characterized by repeating the same path after equal time intervals, known as the period. The pendulum’s 2‑second repeat time exemplifies this. Option B states the correct definition. Option A contradicts the definition of periodic motion, option C is false because the motion does repeat, and option D is unrelated to the physical concept.
